analysis_rows.segment: Function-level documentation for JavaScript and TypeScript
analysis_rows.positioning: The standard format displayed in IDE hover tooltips; tools like TypeDoc generate API documentation from JSDoc
analysis_rows.key_facts: Used by most IDEs; integration with TypeDoc for API generation; AI tools including Copilot and Cursor can generate from function signatures

analysis_rows.segment: Public-facing developer documentation and API references
analysis_rows.positioning: Generates documentation websites from codebase; Git integration detects when documented code changes and flags documentation for review
analysis_rows.key_facts: Strong for API documentation from OpenAPI specs and getting-started guides; replaces Gitbook and Readme.io as default tool for developer-facing documentation

analysis_rows.segment: Internal knowledge documentation linked to specific code
analysis_rows.positioning: Documentation lives alongside code and links directly to specific files, functions, and lines; detects stale documentation and prompts for updates
analysis_rows.key_facts: Maintains link between code and documentation; AI generates draft documentation from code that humans review and edit; has GitHub integration to flag stale documentation

analysis_rows.segment: Entry point documentation for open-source and internal repositories
analysis_rows.positioning: Most-read piece of documentation in entire project; quality bar increased with AI-assisted generation
analysis_rows.key_facts: Should answer: what does project do, why use over alternatives, how to get running locally, how to contribute, where is full documentation

analysis_rows.positioning: Captures significant architectural decisions with context, decision, and consequences; stored in repository alongside code
analysis_rows.key_facts: Human writes (AI cannot know the why); becomes more important with AI agents making code changes; prevents teams from re-litigating same choices

analysis_rows.value: AI drafts, human edits, alerts on stale
Human writes (AI cannot know the why)

analysis_rows.symptom: Developers historically did not write enough documentation
analysis_rows.cause: Code existed but documentation did not; reverse-engineering intent from implementation was required
analysis_rows.evidence: Historical documentation problem mentioned in the Short Answer section
analysis_rows.fix: AI tools can now generate documentation enthusiastically; focus shifted to accuracy and intent

analysis_rows.symptom: AI-generated documentation is technically incorrect despite being grammatically correct
analysis_rows.cause: AI describes what code appears to do, not what developer intended; misses non-obvious logic and design decisions
analysis_rows.evidence: AI describes what code appears to do vs what was intended; misses edge cases, design decisions, invariants
analysis_rows.fix: Use AI for structural aspects (parameters, return values, examples); invest human judgment in non-obvious behavior and why decisions were made

analysis_rows.symptom: Stale documentation that contradicts code is worse than no documentation
analysis_rows.cause: Documentation was accurate 6 months ago but code changes without documentation update
analysis_rows.evidence: Documentation that was accurate 6 months ago but is now wrong due to code changes actively misleads
analysis_rows.fix: Use tools like Swimm that detect stale documentation or establish convention that documentation must update in same PR as code

analysis_rows.symptom: AI refactoring agents violate architectural intent
analysis_rows.cause: AI does not know why particular architecture was chosen
analysis_rows.evidence: AI agents making sweeping code changes without understanding reasoning behind architectural choices
analysis_rows.fix: ADRs become more important to document reasoning behind choices that AI should respect
